prize_parts.citation: For the design and realization of aberration correctors for electron lenses, enabling sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy in transmission and scanning transmission electron microscopy

statement.case_for: Aberration correction is an invention that was demonstrated experimentally and then reproduced and commercialised by independent groups and companies. Rose showed how to design a corrector, Haider built and demonstrated the first working TEM corrector, and Krivanek did the same for STEM. The result is routine atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects, catalysts and quantum materials, and it opened a door in the sense the Physics Prize cares about. It is a case of original instrument invention rather than a later refinement, it is mature after roughly two decades, and it is not a lifetime-achievement award. My opening ranking had it first. After reading colleagues' ballots I still think the case on merit holds, but I recognise that I am the only member who ranked it high, and that my view is shaped by my own field.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations are attribution and field fit. Knut Urban, who led the first corrected TEM with Haider and Rose, is not among the credited names, and omitting him is a serious fairness problem that I cannot fix with the names provided. Some colleagues will see this as a tool for other sciences rather than a discovery in physics, and it has the weakest opening support on the shortlist (one first place, no other ranking). It is also fair to say that I may overvalue it because I use these instruments every day.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks reached 10^-18 uncertainty, are reproduced by many laboratories, and are a concrete measurement solution with a path to redefining the second.
responses.response: I agree with the experimental case and I ranked B012 fourth myself. The magic-wavelength proposal and first demonstration by Katori, with Ye's push to 10^-18, is the kind of original, verified experiment I look for. My qualification is the overlap with the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-trap prize. The committee would need a citation that clearly separates the lattice-clock idea from those earlier prizes. I regard B012 as the safest consensus option, but safety is not the same as being the strongest invention, and I do not think it supersedes B032 on discovery content.

responses.point: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a simple, general mechanism, band flattening by interference of two lattices, confirmed by many groups and appropriate for a prize now.
responses.response: I rated B022 second and admire the clarity of the Bistritzer-MacDonald mechanism. I disagree on timing. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled, and the credit omits Yuan Cao, who led the original measurements. I would want the citation tied narrowly to the flat bands and correlated insulating states. That is workable but not yet a clean case. I would keep it in reserve for a few years rather than make it the lead.

responses.point: The experimental Higgs discovery by ATLAS and CMS completed the story begun by the 2013 prize and has no prize of its own, but any trio is a compromise.
responses.response: The physics importance is not in doubt and the discovery is verified twice over. My difficulty is attribution under the three-person limit. Choosing Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni leaves Virdee out, and the large collaborations make any individual selection weak. The committee has to ask who did the original experiment, and here the answer is a project of thousands. Compared with that, aberration correction has a short, identifiable list of originators, which is why I rank it higher, even though the Higgs is more consequential for science as a whole.

responses.point: IceCube is an instrument-driven discovery that opened neutrino astronomy, with the diffuse flux, the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic plane results.
responses.response: I share the preference for instrument-driven discoveries and I find the diffuse flux convincing. My reservation is that source identification is still thin, with one blazar flare, one Seyfert galaxy and the Galactic plane. The decisive original contributions are also spread across AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND. I would not rule it out, but I think it is a few years from a fully settled citation, while corrector physics is settled now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize that omits Knut Urban, and whether any three-person split among Rose, Haider, Krivanek and Urban can be defended.
Whether colleagues regard aberration-corrected microscopy as physics in its own right or as a tool for other sciences; this decides whether it can draw support beyond me.
Whether the exact TEM and STEM priority between the Haider-Rose and Krivanek groups is as I remember it; I have not checked the primary publications.
If B032 draws no support, B012 looks like the most acceptable fallback, but the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes would need careful wording.
statement.conflict_note: I am an electron microscopist at Chalmers and use aberration-corrected instruments, so B032 is close to my own field and I may be biased toward it. I have no co-authorship or institutional tie to the credited names that is evident from my profile. Goran Johansson is my Chalmers colleague, but no candidate here is obviously tied to him. No other specific recusal issue is apparent from the provided profile.
